# reblocke/hickams-dictum

Purpose: Stata 18 analysis code and supporting tabular data for "Hickam's Dictum: An Analysis of Multiple Diagnoses."

Canonical article:
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11606-024-09120-y
- PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39467949/
- Journal page: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11606-024-09120-y

Repository:
- GitHub: https://github.com/reblocke/hickams-dictum
- Citation metadata: CITATION.cff
- Human README: README.md
- Agent instructions: AGENTS.md
- Data dictionary: data_dictionary.md and data_dictionary.csv

What is here:
- Hickam Analysis.do: main Stata analysis script.
- Survey_Responses.xlsx: anonymous provider survey export used for the main survey analyses.
- NEJM Cases.xlsx: tabulated NEJM diagnostic teaching cases.
- Published Case Reviews.xlsx: tabulated published case reports and coding notes.
- Makefile: convenience wrapper for running the Stata do-file.

How to run:
- Install Stata 18 and the user-written packages listed in README.md.
- From the repository root, run: make run
- Direct Stata command: stata-mp -b do "Hickam Analysis.do"
- Generated tables, figures, and logs are written under Results and Figures/<Stata date>/.

Data and reuse notes:
- The committed workbooks are intended public/anonymized source data for the article.
- Do not add PHI, private respondent data, credentials, or unpublished manuscript drafts.
- Survey platform administrative fields are dropped by the Stata analysis before modeling.
- Interpret workbook columns with data_dictionary.md or data_dictionary.csv.
- Code is MIT licensed. Author-created text, figures, tables, and data notes are CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted.
- Third-party links, publisher pages, and source articles remain under their original terms.

Machine-reader cautions:
- Do not infer that generated outputs in a local working tree are current unless they were produced by the current commit.
- Do not copy long publisher article text into derived documentation; cite DOI/PubMed and summarize briefly.
- The do-file is intended to run from the repository root and will fail early if required workbooks are missing.
